text:
incident-bot: AUTOPAGE fired: PagerDuty alert PD-3487 -> gpu-node-87 (us-west-2a). Alert: kernel panic detected; kubelet not ready; netns watchdog triggered. Priority: P2.
pagerduty: Incident PD-3487 auto-acked by schedule (oncall-jen). Escalation window started.
oncall-jen: I got the page — looking. Can someone confirm customer impact?
sre-liz: Logs show kernel oops + ECC errors right before panic. Node dropped from cluster ~2m ago.
infra-aaron: pulling serial logs now, attaching gist in a sec.
infra-aaron: gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/gpu-node-87-serial-1757777999 (contains dmesg + nvme SMART)
product-mike: any traffic routed to that node? We had a canary batch pinned to gpu-node-87 earlier today.
sre-liz: Canary pods were on that host. Kube scheduler failed over most pods but some stateful canaries kept retrying and hitting 503s until they rescheduled. Impact: small set of customers on the canary route saw transient 5xxs for ~90s.
cs-amy: I'm seeing 3 customer reports flagged internally about intermittent failures ~10:03-10:05 PT — forwarding to support triage.
oncall-jen: ok next steps: cordon + drain if node reachable; otherwise mark unschedulable and evict. Aaron, can you check serial console and IPMI?
infra-aaron: attaching console tail:
```
[ 1234.567890] NMI: CPU stuck for 23s
[ 1234.567901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4200
[ 1234.568000] kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt
Call Trace:
  dump_stack+0x6d/0x8b
  panic+0x13b/0x2f6
  nvrm_handle_error+0x1c2/0x3b0
```
infra-aaron: NVMe SMART shows rising media errors; probable hardware fault causing GPU driver panic.
sre-liz: node is unresponsive to kubelet health checks (NotReady). Trying `kubectl get nodes gpu-node-87 -o wide`
```
NAME          STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-87   NotReady   <none>   12d   v1.30.2
```
oncall-jen: attempt soft-reboot? If it's kernel panic likely reboot already in progress. If it comes up, we should avoid auto-rejoining cluster until postmortem.
infra-aaron: powercycle via IPMI initiated. `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.0.3.87 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle` -> queued.
incident-bot: Escalation: If unacknowledged after 2m, paging secondary (sre-liz). (auto)
sre-liz: I'm on it, jumping in. Oncall-jen handing off.
oncall-jen: handing off to @sre-liz — I'm moving to keep monitoring customer reports. Please DM if you need me back. :wave: (added reaction :white_check_mark:)
sre-liz: powercycle completed, host ping still intermittent. Serial shows linux panic + watchdog reboot loop. I'm going to cordon and create eviction job for remaining pods to avoid stuck crashloops.
infra-aaron: cordon executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-87` -> node marked Unschedulable.
sre-liz: creating force drain for pods with local storage allowed: `kubectl drain gpu-node-87 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`
```
WARNING: ignoring DaemonSet-managed Pods: kube-proxy, node-exporter
oldservice-canary-xyz evicted
model-server-canary-1 evicted
model-server-canary-2 evicted
```
product-mike: were any production (non-canary) model shards on that host? Need to confirm routing fallback didn't route heavy traffic to cheaper CPU fallback.
sre-liz: quick cluster check: `kubectl get pods -A --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-87` returns empty after drain. No prod model shards remained (scheduler earlier moved them off).
cs-amy: Support notes: customers A, B reported errors; I sent initial email acknowledging incident and letting them know we're mitigating. Will follow up with postmortem link later.
incident-bot: Note: automatic fallback policy triggered for Canary route: requests were routed to model-quantized-cpu-v1 for 95s. Observed latency increase median 2.4x and error rate spike to 4% during fallback window.
product-mike: please capture traces for the fallback window and tie to customer reports. We need to surface this in the postmortem.
sre-liz: capturing logs now. `kubectl logs -l app=model-router -n infra --since=15m` -> saving artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/PD-3487/artifacts/logs.tar.gz
infra-aaron: open RMA with colo for GPU and NVMe. Rack tech inbound ETA 3h. Filing ticket: TKT-9982.
oncall-jen: thanks — what's the status on node rejoin? Are we going to auto-recover or keep it cordoned?
sre-liz: keep cordoned until hardware replacement and validated kernel/drivers. We'll avoid auto-rejoin. Setting node label `maintenance=hardware-failure` and taint to prevent accidental scheduling.
```
kubectl label node gpu-node-87 maintenance=hardware-failure
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-87 gpu-failed=true:NoSchedule
```
product-mike: any customer-visible mitigation steps we should take (rate-limiting, alert banners)?
cs-amy: CS suggests a small banner for affected customers and a follow-up message once RMA confirmed. I'll draft.
oncall-jen: I'll update the incident tracking doc and add impact estimates. Short summary: P2; small number of customers on canary route saw 5xx + latency; automated fallback kept availability but increased latency and error surface.
sre-liz: creating handoff to infra on-call for RMA and hardware diagnostics: assigning to infra-aaron. @infra-aaron please confirm when tech on site and expected node offline window.
infra-aaron: confirmed RMA ticket created; tech ETA 3h, expected replacement and validation 5-6h. Will update this thread with serial logs post-report.
incident-bot: Reminder: automatic post-incident survey scheduled in 72h.
product-mike: tagging for postmortem: owners: @sre-liz (infra/ops lead), @product-mike (product impact), @cs-amy (customer comms).
cs-amy: sent banner draft to legal & comms, ready to publish on signoff.
sre-liz: final operational note: no further action needed from eng-oncall unless node behaves unexpectedly or additional customer reports come in. Handing to infra for hardware replacement.
oncall-jen: thanks team — @sre-liz take over; I'm available if needed.
infra-aaron: acknowledging handoff, will keep thread updated. Turning on hardware monitoring probe for nearby rack units.
product-mike: capture lessons: avoid pinning canary to single host; add multi-availability-zone canary placement rule. Adding JIRA.
cs-amy: I'll follow up with customers and provide timeline once RMA progresses.
incident-bot: Thread closed for eng-oncall — moved to infra workflow. (auto)
